chapterTitle: FBISE Annual Exam Simulator 02 (Unit 12: Coordination & Control)
subject: biology-10

questions.question: Which endocrine gland is located at the base of the brain and known as the master gland? (FBISE Annual 2024)
questions.explanation: The anterior pituitary synthesizes multiple tropic hormones that govern other endocrine organs throughout the body.

questions.question: The hormone responsible for lowering elevated blood glucose levels by promoting glucose uptake into cells is: (FBISE 2023)
questions.explanation: Insulin, secreted by pancreatic beta cells in the islets of Langerhans, facilitates cellular uptake and storage of glucose as glycogen.

questions.question: Which part of the human brain regulates muscle coordination, balance, and fine motor posture? (FBISE 2024)
questions.explanation: The cerebellum coordinates somatic motor commands, calibrating balance and graceful musculoskeletal movements.

questions.question: The vital autonomic centers for cardiac contraction, blood pressure, respiration, and swallowing reside in the:
questions.explanation: The medulla oblongata contains essential vegetative reflex centers that automatically sustain life functions.

questions.question: The emergency fight-or-flight hormone secreted rapidly by the adrenal medulla during acute stress is:
questions.explanation: Epinephrine elevates cardiac rate, dilates respiratory bronchioles, and mobilizes blood glucose during perceived emergencies.

questions.question: What is the primary role of myelin sheath surrounding an axon?

options.B: To electrically insulate the axon and increase the speed of nerve impulse conduction

questions.explanation: Myelin sheaths prevent ion leakage, enabling saltatory conduction where action potentials leap rapidly between nodes of Ranvier.

questions.question: The microscopic specialized junction across which a nerve impulse is transferred chemically between two neurons is the: (FBISE 2022)
questions.explanation: At chemical synapses, neurotransmitters diffuse across the synaptic cleft from presynaptic vesicles to postsynaptic receptors.

questions.question: The photosensitive inner sensory layer of the eye containing rod and cone photoreceptors is the: (FBISE 2021)
questions.explanation: The retina converts light photon stimuli into electrical action potentials via visual pigments in rods and cones.

questions.question: Which coiled structure of the inner ear houses the organ of Corti responsible for acoustic hearing? (FBISE 2023)
questions.explanation: The cochlea transforms mechanical fluid vibrations into acoustic nerve signals through sensory hair cells on the basilar membrane.

questions.question: A dietary deficiency of iodine prevents the normal synthesis of thyroxine, resulting in the clinical condition known as: (FBISE 2024)
questions.explanation: Without iodine, the thyroid cannot produce thyroxine. Elevated TSH causes compensatory thyroid gland hypertrophy (goiter).

questions.question: The optical defect where near objects are focused clearly but distant objects appear blurred is termed:
questions.explanation: In myopia, the focal point falls in front of the retina rather than directly on it, corrected using concave lenses.

questions.question: Which division of the autonomic nervous system promotes resting functions such as digestion and heart rate deceleration?
questions.explanation: The parasympathetic system mediates rest-and-digest responses, slowing heart rate and stimulating digestive secretion.
